title: Classic CNN Architectures: LeNet, VGG, ResNet
overview: The history of CNN design shows how depth, small filters and skip connections made image models both deeper and easier to train.
objectives: Describe the design idea of LeNet, VGG and ResNet
Explain how residual connections ease optimization

method.title: LeNet
method.body: An early small CNN of alternating convolution and pooling layers followed by dense layers, used for digit recognition.

method.title: VGG
method.body: Shows that stacking many 3x3 convolutions is an effective, uniform way to add depth.

method.title: ResNet
method.body: Adds identity shortcuts so each block learns a residual F(x) and outputs x + F(x), giving gradients a direct path.

method.title: Bottlenecks
method.body: 1x1 convolutions reduce and restore channels to keep deep blocks cheap.

pseudocode:
def residual_block(x):
    out = relu(bn(conv3x3(x)))
    out = bn(conv3x3(out))
    return relu(out + x)   # skip connection

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
x = rng.normal(size=(1, 8))
W1 = rng.normal(size=(8, 8)) * 0.1
W2 = rng.normal(size=(8, 8)) * 0.1
relu = lambda a: np.maximum(0, a)
F = relu(x @ W1) @ W2
y = relu(x + F)  # residual block
print("input norm: ", round(float(np.linalg.norm(x)), 3))
print("residual norm:", round(float(np.linalg.norm(F)), 3))
print("output norm:", round(float(np.linalg.norm(y)), 3))
